top.title: Multiple planes diverted as bomb threats to commercial flights reported across Europe – as it happened
top.summary: French prime minister’s office says Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome now heading to military base in Evreux The plane appears to have just touched down in Evreux, according to Flightradar24’s tracking service. We will no doubt hear more from authorities in due course.

articles.title: Bomb Threats Disrupt European Flights and Rattle Passengers
articles.summary: Passengers recounted landing at a military base and being subjected to security checks and travel delays after threats that turned out to be hoaxes affected planes in Italy, Poland, Spain.

edits.title: Passengers Tell of Fear After Bomb Threats Hit European Flights

articles.title: Multiple flights in Europe diverted because of bomb threats after earlier hoaxes
articles.summary: Multiple flights in Europe made emergency landings on Thursday after being diverted because of bomb threats. The incidents followed hoax bomb threats earlier this week that prompted searches, diversions and in one case a military escort.

articles.title: Bomb threats disrupt at least 25 flights across Europe, raising hybrid war fears
articles.summary: Planes forced into emergency landings or diversions two days after hoax alerts affected air travel Europe live – latest updates Bomb threats have caused diversions and emergency landings for at least 15 flights across Europe , renewing questions about a possibly coordinated effort to disrupt travel. The series of warnings on Thursday morning affected flights between Italy, Ireland, the UK, Spain, Bulgaria, Romania, Poland, Finland, Austria, Denmark, Belgium, Portugal, Greece and Czechia.

articles.title: Bomb threats cause major flight disruptions across Europe
articles.summary: Bomb ​threats forced airliners to make unplanned landings across Europe on Thursday morning, the latest in a series of threats targeting flights in Europe. While no country has attributed blame for the threats, they come at a time ​when European officials have been blaming both Russia and Iran for what they describe as "hybrid attacks" and acts of sabotage. Moscow and Tehran both deny any such campaign. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle tells us more.

articles.title: Bomb threats disrupt several flights across Europe
articles.summary: At least a dozen flights were either diverted or landed with a military escort after bomb or security threats. The first reported case involved a flight from Dublin to Rome landing outside Paris and more soon followed.
